[b][u]STARBOUND RP[/u]

Operation Scoria I[/b]

In all things but name, the League of the Orange Creek was a sovereign country. Officially it was just an alliance of corporations working under the Vespurian Empire, and through it the Federation. However, both the Empire and the Federation are nowhere to be seen, and so the League effectively conducts its own affairs without opposition from the powers that be.

No place is this better seen than in its immense armed forces known as the Central Security Group, or better known as the Orange Guard. Just like how the League pretends to just be a corporation, the Orange Guard pretends to be a security service. But you don't really see security services operating massive warships or using cloning technology, do you? Nor do you see security guards with formalized rank structures, organized into infantry commands, never mind a bloody hymn.

The Orange Guard fights its battles on land, sea, air, and space. Among these, space has been the most prominent, particularly in the aftermath of the Marisalbic War. During the war, the Orange Guard was more of an [i]ad hoc[/i] arrangement between the Vespurian Convention Party, SummitONE Solutions, and El Howayek Group.

Nowadays though, the Conventionists have lost their relevance, while the El Howayeks opted to focus on civilian industry and circular economy. As far as the Ardagan System is concerned, SummitONE was analogous to the Orange Guard.

This gave SummitONE exceptional operational autonomy over the League when it came to military matters, which has led to quite a lot of tension between it and the El Howayeks, who've regularly accused SummitONE of instigating foreign conflicts to drive up interest in its technologies. Of course, SummitONE would never do this. Wars were bad for business after all. The impact of just a single death on a household was immense enough to paralyze their consumer spending.

So, what if we had a way of circumventing death itself?

Not through immortality, though we're working on that, but rather on getting others to fight the wars for you?

- - -

[b]7 January 2176

VCV [i]Exemplar[/i], three kilometers away from the ONC [i]Orange Creek[/i][/b]

Beyond the O'Neill Cylinders of the Orange Creek hovered two colossal spacecraft. Super-battleships, they were officially called, though they were really just space stations with lasers and various armaments strapped onto them. At around 500 meters in length, they were among the largest ships in the Ardagan System, though only by technicality, with detractors often noting that they served more like military installations or point defenses than actual spacecraft.

And yet, the super-battleships moved. They could maneuver under their own propulsion systems, though not very quickly.

One of these two behemoths was a venerable ship known as the [i]Exemplar[/i], formerly a Federation vessel used by the Multinational Force to depart from Erene during the darkest periods following the Disaster Year. Despite the destructive attack that nearly destroyed the vessel and killed half its complement, the [i]Exemplar [/i]miraculously survived, trudging along by its own power before settling in Lagrange Point 4, where it stays to this day, quietly guarding over the O'Neill Cylinders with a awesome gaze.

In the distance, a tiny shuttle pod emerged out of the abyss of space, docking beside the [i]Exemplar[/i], its clamps engaging the [i]Exemplar [/i]with a resonant thud before being pulled into its cavernous interior.

As the [i]Exemplar [/i]slowly sealed itself, a blonde-haired, pale-faced woman stepped out of the shuttle pod and look around her. "I'm here.", the woman muttered, speaking into a device embedded into her armor. She then walked deeper into the ship, tilting her head every so often to listen to the low, rhythmic humming of the fusion drives and life-support recyclers. Crew members in utilitarian jumpsuits paused their duties to stare, but she pressed on, navigating the sterile corridors toward the fitting stations.

[list]"You must be the clone." said one of the technicians, easily recognizing the NSI's black armor.  "NSI3-4 if I'm remembering things correctly. A shame you folks will be leaving so soon. Us taxpayers spent a hefty sum just for y'all, the least you coulda done would be to stick around."

"Is Frame 167 ready?" NSI3-4 replied, ignoring the soldier's commentary.

"... Yeah, she is... look, just remember, this isn't a regular combat mission, this is a test run. Even if you feel like it's not optimal, SummitONE wants you to use [i]everything[/i] the suit has to offer, alright?"[/list]

The clone nodded mechanically before turning to look at the source of the corporate world's ruckus. Placed into the floor of the fitting station was a large, humanoid construct, like a sort of droid, but the size of a telephone pole. It was a mobile suit, one of the very first of its kind to be manufactured by a Federation polity. This particular series was called the S1S NCS Belezan, or "Frame 167", for it was formally registered with the League on the 1st of January 2167, New Year's Day.

From a glance, the Belezan appeared no different from your typical droid trooper, just upscaled to fit a human pilot. Its armor was no different from the usual tank armor, painted black to match with NSI3-4's own black-plated power armor. The Belezan carried a small, custom gun on its right hand, effectively a plasma rifle, while it used a shield on its left for close-quarters combat. On its broad shoulders were sets of rocket launchers, like the kind used in naval SAMs, while nearer to the mech's "head" were a number of smaller caliber autocannons for use against ground targets and lightly-armored spacecraft.

[list]"What do you think?" asked the technician, waiting to see if the clone's prying eyes were satisfied by the mobile suit's condition.[/list]

Rather than answering, NSI3-4 nodded mechanically and climbed into the Belezan's cockpit, its neural interfaces syncing with her cloned physiology for seamless control. The process was meticulous. First, a medical scan to confirm her vitals, drawing a small blood sample recycled into the ship's biomass converters, the Belezan's internal computer affirming that she was ready to pilot the machine. Around her, the bay buzzed with activity as the [i]Exemplar [/i]became notified that the first of three Belezans was now being manned. 

Technicians scrambled to make some last minute adjustments, engineers fine-tuned the mobile suit's thrusters recycled from asteroid-sourced alloys, nutrient packs were checked and rechecked for the clone's use. Scrap metal from adjustments was melted down on-site, coolant fluids purified through membrane filters, and even the technicians' waste breaks timed to align with the ship's reclamation cycles.

All the while, in the distance, a large carrier ship slowly began to approach and prepare to dock against the [i]Exemplar[/i]. It had been painted over completely black to make its identifications impossible to know, but the [i]Exemplar's[/i] captain nevertheless easily identified the strange vessel by its true name, [i]Kipsaga.[/i]

- - -

[b]15 January 2176

VCV [i]Kipsaga[/i], Somewhere in the Belt of Tears[/b]

The VCV [i]Kipsaga [/i]weaved carefully through the Belt of Tears, carrying only a skeleton crew of 35 people. At over 25 kilotons in mass and some 312 meters in diameter, the [i]Kipsaga [/i]was one of the larger spacecraft in active military service. 

As a [i]Wayfinder[/i]-class, one could easily surmise the ship to be a Federation vessel, though prior to departing from the [i]Exemplar[/i], the [i]Kipsaga [/i]had undergone heavy modifications to make itself virtually unrecognizable from Federation vessels. Exterior fuel tanks had been refitted to different sections of the hull, different thruster designs had been used, even the thermal radiators were modified to resemble the kind used by Spacenoids living in the hostility of deep space.

However, the [i]Kipsaga [/i]didn't traverse through the Belt, some half a billion kilometers, just to play a crude prank on an unsuspecting commercial vessel, for embedded within the carrier's compartment was an atmospheric entry vehicle, and within it was a Frame 167 Belezan mobile suit, fully armed, fueled, and polished to perfection, waiting patiently for its first and final mission.

In Aceldama, homeland of the Aceldixan Confederacy, fleet sensors would manage to spot the bright orange radiators of an unknown ship approaching from beyond the darkness of outer space.

[/spoiler]
